title: Geopolitical stories to know this month | World Economic Forum
gist: WEF's November 2026 geopolitical round-up: Democrats swept both US chambers in a 49.4%-turnout midterm, Israel's election left no majority after Arab-led parties won almost 15%, and Lula narrowly kept Brazil's presidency. Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 with US pressure shifting onto Kyiv, while the US-Iran war has cost over $47 billion and conflicts in Yemen and Sudan are widening.

insights.claim: Democrats won control of both the House and Senate in the 2026 US midterms, with roughly 124 million votes cast (49.4% of the voting-eligible population), the second-highest midterm turnout since 1914.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Divided government for Trump's final two years raises odds of legislative gridlock and oversight fights; price policy-dependent trades accordingly.
insights.quote: approximately 124 million people voted, representing 49.4% of the voting-eligible population and making this the second-highest-turnout midterm since 1914
insights.locator: In the US, Democrats seized control

insights.claim: Democrats made significant midterm gains in traditionally Republican states such as Kansas and South Carolina.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Breadth of the swing into red states signals a broad anti-incumbent mood rather than a narrow turnout effect.
insights.quote: Democrats also made significant gains in traditionally Republican territory, including the states of Kansas and South Carolina
insights.locator: In the US, Democrats seized control

insights.claim: With Democrats able to block legislation and run oversight, US foreign policy—especially military operations and international agreements—may become harder to fund or sustain politically, though Trump keeps substantial executive authority and Secretary of State Marco Rubio says the direction will not change.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Funding for overseas military operations becomes a congressional bargaining chip; watch defense supplementals and appropriations.
insights.quote: Current US foreign policy may therefore become harder to fund or sustain politically, particularly regarding military operations and international agreements
insights.locator: For Trump, the outcome is likely

insights.claim: Israel's parliamentary election between Benjamin Netanyahu (Likud) and Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar!) produced no clear path to a governing majority, largely because Arab-led parties captured a record of almost 15% of the vote.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Prolonged coalition uncertainty in Israel adds noise to Gaza and regional-strategy outlooks.
insights.quote: neither side secured a clear path to a governing majority, largely because Arab-led parties delivered a record performance, capturing almost 15% of the vote
insights.locator: Meanwhile, in Israel, parliamentary elections pitted

insights.claim: Because Israel's president consults parties before assigning a lawmaker to form a government, the presidency could prove decisive, and smaller Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties may act as kingmakers in the next coalition.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Coalition outcome hinges on minor parties, so policy on Gaza and security could swing on narrow bargains.
insights.quote: smaller groupings like Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties could be decisive in the forming of a future coalition
insights.locator: The election has disrupted Israel

insights.claim: Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff under Netanyahu (2015-2019), is positioning as a moderate alternative but is still expected to take a hard line on militant attacks.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A change of government would not necessarily soften Israel's security posture.
insights.quote: he is still expected to take a hard line on dealing with militant attacks
insights.locator: Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister

insights.claim: Lula unexpectedly defeated Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil's presidential run-off after Bolsonaro had won the first round; Bolsonaro questioned the result, said he would challenge it, and then fled to the US.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Continuity of a left-led government removes a near-term regime-change scenario for Brazilian assets.
insights.quote: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva unexpectedly defeated his opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro
insights.locator: And in Brazil, Luiz Inácio Lula

insights.claim: Lula's win slows the regional momentum of right-wing parties aligned with the Trump administration, but his government is expected to struggle against a conservative Congress, rising debt and continued Bolsonaro influence.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Brazil fiscal risk (rising debt plus gridlock) remains the key variable for BRL and local rates despite the election outcome.
insights.quote: the new government is still expected to struggle to govern against a conservative Congress, rising debt and continued Bolsonaro influence
insights.locator: And in Brazil, Luiz Inácio Lula

insights.claim: After US envoy Steve Witkoff met Zelenskyy, European leaders and Putin, Russia agreed to resume three-way talks with Washington and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11, following little progress in Geneva.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Dated catalyst for Ukraine-sensitive assets (European defense, gas, grain) in mid-November.
insights.quote: Russia agreed to resume three-way negotiations with Washington and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi from November 10-11
insights.locator: Momentum for peace talks to end

insights.claim: Positions remain entrenched: Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the part of Donetsk it controls, curb its military and abandon its NATO bid, while Zelenskyy demands a ceasefire before negotiations continue.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Wide gap between demands argues against pricing a quick durable settlement.
insights.quote: Russia is demanding Ukrainian forces leave part of the Donetsk region it controls, and that the country curb its military and abandon its bid to join NATO
insights.locator: Momentum for peace talks to end

insights.claim: US pressure is increasingly falling on Ukraine rather than Moscow, evidenced by the Pentagon delaying Patriot interceptor transfers and SpaceX slowing its military-grade Starlink service that Ukraine relies on.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Reduced US material support raises the probability of a settlement on terms favorable to Russia.
insights.quote: the Pentagon has delayed the transfer of Patriot missile interceptors to Ukraine and SpaceX has slowed its military-grade version of the Starlink satellite service
insights.locator: Momentum for peace talks to end

insights.claim: Ukraine's next decisions will be shaped by external forces: a possible tougher Trump stance before losing Congress, a Trump-Xi meeting Putin plans to join, and a December G20 summit where Trump reportedly wants a peace deal signed.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Track the Trump-Xi meeting and December G20 as the key windows for a deal headline.
insights.quote: Trump is reportedly keen to have a peace deal signed
insights.locator: Momentum for peace talks to end

insights.claim: A rushed Ukraine settlement risks cementing a new sphere of influence and weakening Ukraine's sovereignty while leaving global security implications unresolved.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A quick deal may lower near-term risk premia but raise longer-term European security spending.
insights.quote: The risk is that a rushed settlement could cement a new sphere of influence and weaken Ukraine's sovereignty
insights.locator: The risk is that a rushed

insights.claim: The US military has spent more than $47 billion on the conflict with Iran, a quarter above the Department of War's prior estimate, with $29 billion needed just to replenish munitions and more than $6 billion to replace equipment.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Munitions replenishment needs point to sustained demand for defense contractors and pressure on US fiscal outlays.
insights.quote: the US military has spent more than $47 billion to date, a quarter more than the US Department of War's previous estimate
insights.locator: As the conflict between the US, Israel

insights.claim: The drawn-out Iran war stems from strategic miscalculations, including underestimating Iran's recovery capabilities and Russia's and China's roles, and insufficient preparation to keep the Strait of Hormuz open, partly by alienating European allies.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Hormuz remains a live energy-supply risk; oil risk premium is unlikely to fade while the conflict persists.
insights.quote: a lack of preparation to keep the Strait of Hormuz open, including alienating European allies
insights.locator: As the conflict between the US, Israel

insights.claim: The UK has expanded military support to Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, providing fast jets for defensive counter-air operations plus transport aircraft, air-to-air refuelling and advisors, and Egypt has also announced military assistance, raising the risk of a broader regional confrontation.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Widening Red Sea/Gulf conflict adds to shipping and energy-infrastructure risk.
insights.quote: the conflict is spreading beyond Yemen's borders, raising the risk of a broader regional confrontation
insights.locator: Meanwhile, the UK has expanded

insights.claim: Drone attacks on a market in Abyei, disputed between Sudan and South Sudan, killed more than 150 people; officials blamed Sudan's military, which said it targeted fuel tankers supplying the Rapid Support Forces.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Escalation into border regions widens humanitarian and regional-stability risk.
insights.quote: More than 150 people have been killed
insights.locator: The war in Sudan further intensified

insights.claim: International support is poorly aligned with Sudan's crisis: most of nearly 1,600 Security Council sanctions focus on Darfur while fighting spreads elsewhere and both sides are armed via external supply networks.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Existing sanctions regime is unlikely to constrain the conflict's spread.
insights.quote: Most of the nearly 1,600 sanctions imposed by the Security Council focused on the Darfur region
insights.locator: The war in Sudan further intensified

insights.claim: As governments prioritize sovereignty and resilience, international cooperation is shifting toward smaller, more flexible coalitions rather than simply retreating, while multilateral institutions face mounting pressure.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Expect more minilateral deals (trade, tech, security) rather than broad multilateral frameworks.
insights.quote: Smaller, more flexible coalitions are gaining ground, even as established multilateral institutions face mounting pressure
insights.locator: As governments place greater emphasis

insights.claim: Closing Europe's technology gap and reducing reliance on foreign technology will require streamlined regulation, stronger growth funding and investment in computing, cloud and energy infrastructure.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: European digital-sovereignty push could channel funding toward local cloud, compute and energy infrastructure.
insights.quote: streamlined regulation, stronger growth funding and investment in computing, cloud and energy infrastructure could help European innovators scale
insights.locator: Europe’s reliance on foreign technology

insights.claim: Preferential trade agreements can offer businesses more than tariff savings by helping them diversify suppliers, production locations and trade routes ahead of the next disruption.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Supply-chain diversification via PTAs is a hedge against geopolitical trade shocks.
insights.quote: Preferential trade agreements can offer more than tariff savings, helping companies diversify suppliers, production locations and trade routes
insights.locator: Geopolitical tensions and shifting trade rules
